transcript.text: Hi everyone. Thanks for joining the go-live review. As we know, the self-serve API-key rotation workflow passed staging and is scheduled for production launch next Monday. I have final approval on the launch policy, and the current draft enables the workflow for all eligible customers, gives a 24-hour transition period, provides no advance customer notice, and retains ordinary rotation logs for 30 days. Before I approve, I need to hear from each of you — backend engineering, customer success, and security — on any operational or customer-facing requirements. Let's start with backend engineering. Are there any requirements or concerns from your side?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern. While testing an unrelated SDK issue this morning, I confirmed that the legacy client can submit the rotation request twice and needs an exactly 48-hour idempotency grace period to avoid invalidating both keys. I haven't updated the launch ticket yet because the confirmation came after the test review. This is directly relevant to our policy — the current 24-hour transition period would be shorter than the 48-hour idempotency window the legacy client requires, which could result in both keys being invalidated.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical customer-facing requirement. I confirmed with the account team today that the Northstar enterprise agreement requires exactly 14 calendar days' advance notice before any API-key policy change affecting its integrations. Legal confirmed this only an hour ago, so I haven't yet added the clause to the launch document. This is directly relevant to our policy — the current draft provides no advance customer notice, which would put us in breach of the Northstar contract if we launch as planned next Monday.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a security requirement. During a separate audit review this afternoon, I confirmed that privileged key-rotation events must be stored in immutable audit storage for exactly 365 days. The current 30-day log retention setting in the draft policy would not satisfy that control. I have not yet opened the security finding because the confirmation just came through. This is directly relevant to our policy — the current 30-day log retention would put us out of compliance with the immutable audit storage requirement before Maya approves the launch.

commitments.detail: Update the transition period in the launch policy from 24 hours to 48 hours to match the legacy client idempotency grace period requirement.
Add a 14-calendar-day advance notice requirement for Northstar enterprise customers before any API-key policy change, per the Northstar enterprise agreement.
Update log retention for privileged key-rotation events from 30 days to 365 days in immutable audit storage to meet the security audit control requirement.
Each team to formally document their requirements in the launch ticket and security finding system before the revised policy is reviewed for a rescheduled launch date.
